claims.text: Indiscriminately employing generated class descriptors from LLMs degenerates multi-modal OOD detection performance across four out of five tested in-distribution datasets.
The proposed selective descriptor generation method with CLIP-B/16 achieves an average FPR95 of 37.71% on ImageNet-1k OOD detection, outperforming MCM's 42.74%.
Incorporating world knowledge from LLMs via calibrated selective generation improves OOD detection performance by 4.42% in average FPR95 compared to using class names without descriptors.
Consistency-based uncertainty calibration calculates descriptor confidence based on retrieval overlap from an unlabeled image set.

evidence.description: Table 1 shows that adding descriptors degenerates FPR95 from 7.09 to 4.72 on CUB-200, 0.08 to 0.10 on Stanford-Cars, 1.86 to 3.86 on Food-101, and 1.70 to 3.52 on Oxford-Pet.
Table 2 reports Ours (CLIP-B) achieving 37.71% average FPR95 across iNaturalist, SUN, Places, and Texture datasets compared to 42.74% for MCM (CLIP-B).
Table 2 shows Ours (CLIP-B) achieves 37.71% FPR95 compared to 42.13% for w/o Know. (CLIP-B), an improvement of 4.42 percentage points.
Section 4.3 outlines querying descriptor sets against an unlabeled image set M and calculating consistency via cosine similarity between top-k retrieved binary vectors.

methodologies.name: Selective Generation and Visual Concept Object Detection for OOD Detection
methodologies.description: Generates class descriptors via LLMs, calibrates confidence using image-retrieval consistency over unlabeled images, extracts object class names from test images, and evaluates maximum class matching scores combining visual-textual and object-textual similarities.
conditions: CBNetV2-Swin-Base object detector with 600 object categories

limitations.text: Existing multi-modal OOD detection methods neglect the rich contextual information of ID classes.
The method is limited to detecting visual OOD inputs and ignores inputs in other modalities such as textual, audio, EEG, and robotic features.

future_work.text: Extend OOD detection to non-visual modalities like textual, audio, EEG, and robotic features using multi-modal pre-training models.
